analysis.title: CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV) 3Q26: New contract economics and visibility into financing is first step in stock rerating
key_insights: CRWV is up 8% after hours after reporting 3Q26 revenue 3% above the Street and EBIT margin 350bps above Street (Visible Alpha). 4Q implied revenue guidance is 3% above the Street, margin 100bps above, and capex 22% below.

Financing plan: no additional parent-level unsecured debt through 2027. The significant majority of remaining capital needs are expected to be funded through delayed-draw term loans (DDTLs) that can finance 70%-100% of associated capex at 7-10% yields.
Other funding levers are customer prepayments, OEM financing and growing operating cash flow. GS sees a path to funding growth with less than $5bn of incremental parent capital through 2027.
4-5 year contracts now price at $20-$25mn per MW, against WholeCo revenue of about $10mn per MW and capex of about $40mn per MW. Shorter-duration opportunities reach about $40mn per MW.
On these economics GS estimates post-tax unlevered IRR of 20-30% before residual value, against 15-21% prior.

About 130k GPUs roll off contract in 2027 and about 170k in 2028. At current pricing, management estimates the 2027 renewals could generate nearly $4bn of annualized revenue, rising to nearly $10bn including 2028, with no incremental capex.

Asset-level secured financing has priced at SOFR +225bps to +550bps since the IPO, with IG customer contracts at the tight end and AI labs toward the wide end. At current rates that implies 7-7.5% for IG-backed facilities and under 10% at the high end.
More than 75% of committed 2027 capex not yet attached to an existing DDTL is tied to IG and enterprise customers.

Prepayments appear in about 70% of deals this year, with penetration expected to rise. About $9bn is due from signed contracts over the next three months, including about $3bn against existing, already funded infrastructure.
GS argues the success-based capex model, which ties deployments to signed customer contracts, mitigates the 2027 oversupply bear case. Current pricing and recontracting suggest demand remains tight.

GS does not include a model update, pending more detail in the 10Q. Rating is Buy with a $106 12-month price target based on 18x SNTM EBIT (Q5-Q8), implying 117.5% upside from $48.73. The stock is down 53.9% over 12 months.
GS would add to positions with the stock near YTD lows, citing technology differentiation, ability to scale capex and favorable contract economics as drivers of equity returns over 12 months.

market_movers.rationale: GS would add to positions near YTD lows. It sees contract economics and financing visibility as the first step in a rerating, with uIRR of 20-30% before residual value.

earnings_insights: CRWV 3Q26 actual (reported 11/10) revenue $3,661mn vs GSe $3,535mn and Street $3,557mn (Visible Alpha consensus), +4% vs GSe and +3% vs Street, +168% y/y.
3Q26 actual operating income $379mn vs GSe $236mn and Street $245mn, +60% vs GSe and +55% vs Street. Margin was 10% vs 7% for both GSe and Street.
3Q26 actual capex including finance leases $14,511mn vs GSe $12,737mn and Street $12,121mn.
3Q26 actual free cash flow was -$7,466mn vs GSe -$11,049mn and Street -$9,116mn.
4Q implied revenue guidance is 3% above the Street, margin 100bps above, capex 22% below.

GS holds estimates unchanged pending the 10Q. Existing GS estimates: revenue $12,960mn for 2026E, $27,529mn for 2027E, $47,535mn for 2028E. EPS is -$3.80 for 2026E and -$2.34 for 2027E, turning to $3.36 for 2028E.
GS quarterly EPS estimates: 9/26E -$1.11, 12/26E -$0.56, 3/27E -$0.79. The 6/26 figure is -$1.03.

trade_ideas.description: Buy CRWV stock near YTD lows, 12-month price target $106 (18x SNTM EBIT, Q5-Q8)
trade_ideas.rationale: Contract economics improve (uIRR 20-30% before residual value) and the financing plan gains visibility.
trade_ideas.risk: Issues with raising financing, ramping data center capacity, timing mismatches between contract pricing and cost inflation, or pricing degrading on new contracts or renewals.

risk_factors: Timing mismatches between where contracts are struck and cost inflation to bring them online.
Supply/demand dynamics such that pricing degrades on new contracts or renewals.
Investor debate over 2027 demand as large amounts of new supply come online and compute gets more efficient.

tension_points.bull_case: Success-based capex ties deployments to signed, underwritten customer contracts. Renewal pricing of $20-$25mn/MW sits above the fleet's roughly $10mn/MW revenue today, so demand remains tight.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors debate the 2027 demand function as large amounts of new supply come online and compute gets more efficient, which could degrade pricing on new contracts or renewals.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Pricing degrading on new contracts or renewals, or issues raising financing (GS key risks).

theme_stances.key_argument: Contract pricing of $20-$25mn/MW and DDTL funding at 7-10% lift unlevered returns well above WACC.
theme_stances.evidence: would add to positions with the stock near YTD lows
